title: GraphPilot workspace direction
question: Choose a visual direction for the repository workspace.

options.label: Architectural atlas
options.thesis: A calm repository workspace with traceable relationships and precise source references.
options.viewport: A familiar navigation rail, repository header, graph workspace and source-evidence panel.
options.risk: Dense graphs need progressive disclosure to stay legible.

raised.raise: Job updates keep their alignment as status changes.
A decisive type hierarchy separates context from evidence.
Selected evidence is unambiguous at every depth.
Repository and branch context remain visible.
Focus reveals useful detail without hiding the task.

options.label: Technical publication
options.thesis: A restrained workspace built around clear explanations and source excerpts.
options.viewport: A compact rail and broad graph with a document-like evidence column.
options.risk: Familiar developer-product styling may feel less distinctive.

options.label: Orienteering legend
options.thesis: Typed graph colors and one strong selection color make complex relationships readable.
options.viewport: Standard app navigation around a broad graph and ranked evidence list.
options.risk: The diagram palette could become busy on larger graphs.
options.case: Strong graph clarity; architectural references fit the developer audience more closely.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: A source-world study translated into standard app components.
options.viewport: Navigation, repository context, graph and evidence.
options.risk: The metaphor competes with the investigation task.
options.case: Weaker developer identification and evidence clarity.
